processing: Sun-dried sheng maocha, kept loose or pressed, with no ripe-style fermentation.
harvest_season: Spring is the prized picking, as elsewhere in Yiwu.
appearance_dry: Tight, even, dark and lustrous strands, at least from the Wangong garden.
appearance_liquor: Golden, at least from the Wangong garden.
taste_profile: Little is documented for the village as a whole. Tea from its Wangong garden is described as high and pure in aroma, with a golden liquor; typical of Yiwu, expect a soft body and a sweet return.

brewing.notes: Rinse once and keep early steeps short; aged cakes can take a little longer from the start.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year, like other sheng, both young and with some age. A published spring price index split it into village-side small-tree leaf at 500 yuan per kilogram and old-tree leaf at 1,500 to 1,600, so ask which you are buying. Yao and Han village teas may be named separately.
description:
Dingjiazhai is really two neighbouring communities in the Yiwu area, one Yao and one Han, listed separately among Yiwu's eight stockaded villages. It lies across the Lengshui river from Guafengzhai, up steep mountain roads from Mahei, and its gardens reach to the well-known Wangong.

The tea is ordinary sheng in method. The people and old trees here make it worth a look, and it belongs to the group of remote eastern Yiwu names that drinkers look for.

Expect fragrant, smooth Yiwu. Tasting notes are few, and a difference between Yao and Han lots is not something the sources settle, so a side-by-side tasting is yours to try.

When buying, ask whether the leaf is from around the village or from the older gardens, since prices differ sharply. Much of the nearby land has gone over to rubber, which limits what real old-tree leaf exists.
history:
Han Dingjiazhai lies on a listed stretch of the old tea-horse road in Mengla, as does a road to the lower Yao settlement, so the village was tied to the tea trade through Yiwu. No founding date for the gardens is documented.

The name reached wider attention with the single-mountain pu-erh market. A 2009 Yunnan Sourcing cake named Road to Yi Wu Ding Jia Zhai is one example on the Western market. In recent years the village has also become a collecting point for tea from around it.
